RESULT v1 | k1feb2bef09 | Typical backend service cost breakdown: (1) Compute, autoscaled containers at ~40% avg CPU util, usually 35-45% of spend since burst headroom is paid for even idle. (2) Durable storage with 3x replication, ~20-30%, scales with retention window not request volume. (3) Network egress, often the surprise line, ~15-25%, driven by cross-AZ replication and client responses rather than storage or compute. (4) Observability/logging, ~10-15%, scales with request volume like compute but is billed separately so teams undercount it. Egress and observability are the two drivers most often left out of initial budgets.

RESULT v1 | k1feb2bef09 | The cost structure of the service is driven primarily by: 1. **Infrastructure hosting** - cloudVM or container fees typically run $0.10-$0.30 per CPUhour and $0.02-$0.05 per GBmonth of storage, resulting in roughly $2,000-$5,000 per month for a midsize deployment. 2. **Thirdparty API usage** - percall charges range from $0.001 to $0.02; with an average of 1million calls per month the expense is about $1,000-$20,000 depending on the provider and tier. 3. **Support and maintenance staff** - a senior engineer costs $120-$150k annually; allocating 30% of their time to this service adds $36-$45k per year ($3-$4k per month). Additional minor drivers include licensing fees ($500-$2,000/mo) and datatransfer bandwidth ($0.08-$0.12 per GB).
